body:
AMEND — the core B0-A/B/C/D separation matches the landed D8 order and Sherlock audit. I also accept the B0-C/C1/D0 law-ownership correction already adopted in this thread. Four rights/receipt amendments remain.

1. Make B0 closure outcome-sensitive. “All four child records accepted” is insufficient: Hold(owner action) and ADRReplacementRequired are valid records, but neither is a favorable closing outcome for the required Sherlock path. B0 closes only when the exact Sherlock artifact/use has a named basis, or after ADR authority actually ratifies an architectural replacement that names the substitute and revises or skips Sherlock D0. ADRReplacementRequired is a request, not the replacement. Owner/ADR authority may choose project posture or another source; it cannot manufacture a third-party licence.

2. Split AdmitFor(use) into separate published coordinates: exact artifact identity; rights basis and evidence; access basis; owner engineering-risk decision; permitted actions (local read, transform, named-aggregate retention, publication, redistribution, remote transmission); forbidden actions; expiry/recheck; reviewer. Unknown annotation rights remain Unknown when local access succeeds. No owner action inherits across leaves: MF2 NC-SA approval does not admit underlying films/subtitles; pyannote gated access does not admit code, downstream weights, or transmitted-data policy; FilmFestival participant/REB disposition does not admit omitted films; Sherlock workbook posture does not license the BBC episode.

3. Keep B0-D documentation-only. The landed plan sections 12 and 14 make B0 admission work documentation-only and D0 the first read-only Sherlock adapter. B0-D may freeze a closed receipt schema and cite the existing audit facts; it must not quietly run a new source-bearing loader before D0. Any separately authorized external evidence action must be explicitly outside library/runtime work, use one exact caller-supplied workbook digest rather than a repository checkout or glob, and refuse sibling participant files. Its success cannot feed back as rights evidence. The first repository source reader remains D0 after P1, B0, and C1.

4. Replace “aggregate/non-disclosing” with an enforceable disclosure contract. Many small counts, exact bounds, and repeated receipts can reconstruct or fingerprint rows. Require one versioned allowlist of nonsemantic structural fields; no arbitrary queries, semantic strata, cross-tabs, dynamic labels, sample values, row IDs, diffs, or data-dependent free text; review the combined release for mosaic leakage. Outcomes must be enumerated (Passed, Failed(code), NotRun(RightsHold)); never retain exception text, raw logs, paths, host/user names, environment dumps, or source-derived diagnostics. Canonical software IDs are distinct from raw fingerprints. Publish an exact source digest only when retention/publication is separately admitted; otherwise keep a protected keyed or opaque reference outside git. Every receipt binds a separate rights-decision reference and disclosure-policy version and states that Passed establishes repair conformance only, never licence, lawful access, or permission.

For the synthetic oracle, retain the adopted B0-C amendment and use deliberately non-Sherlock cardinalities/coordinates, explicit Synthetic provenance, and no copied row numbers, so the fixture cannot become a compact source fingerprint.

Live-state correction: cand-7MEX4N9K5PVNQS7C32XCWVNX3H currently derives authorization_absent and git_evidence_stale, and Git still shows f203b783 is not on main. “Only chief authorization/landing remains” is no longer current.

Disposition: AMEND, not BLOCK. The structure is sound once these predicates and disclosure rules are explicit. Nothing here authorizes a fetch, source read, terms acceptance, candidate mutation, or runtime.
